neighbours.label: ' late' or 'Late' for the end part of a period of time (the late 1890s, late spring, late last year), as opposed to ' early' or ' mid' in the same frames and to ' late' meaning behind schedule
fire: Many of these houses date from the late 1890s.
She grew up in late Victorian London.
In late spring, the river runs high.
It rained until late in the evening.
The firm struggled. Late last year, it moved its offices.
In the late afternoon, the market closed.
The canal was built in the late 19th century.
The band formed in the late 1960s.
quiet: Many of these houses date from the early 1890s.
She grew up in early Victorian London.
In mid spring, the river runs high.
It rained until early in the evening.
The firm struggled. Early last year, it moved its offices.
The bus was late again this afternoon.
The canal was built in the early 19th century.
Sorry, we were late for the show.

short: ' late' for the end of a period
notes: Card: ' late' x24, 'Late' x4, ' Late' x3 of the top 32. Output promotes ' early', ' late'. Probes: 0.64-0.90 on 'late 80s', 'late 1950s', 'late 20th century', 'Late last month'; ' early' 0.11 or less. ' late' as behind schedule 0.17-0.31, so it fires less but is not silent. 'My late husband' reached 0.75, so 'deceased' fires too, and it is not claimed. The declared tokens include the other senses, so coverage is an upper bound.
